[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This facility, Switch Las Vegas 4, is part of Switch Las Vegas Core Campus in Clark County, Nevada, spanning locations including Las Vegas, Enterprise, and near McCarran. Switch was founded in 2000 by Rob Roy, who serves as CEO and chief engineer, and the company is headquartered in Las Vegas. Wikipedia coverage states that in 2002 Roy acquired a former Enron facility in Las Vegas at auction for 930,000 dollars, strategically located over a fiber optic backbone serving technology companies nationwide, which became the foundation of the Las Vegas Core Campus. That campus has grown to eleven operating data centers spanning over 2 million square feet, with plans to reach 2.3 million square feet across 12 buildings. Switch also operates the Citadel Campus in Storey County in Northern Nevada, a separate 4 billion dollar, 1,000 plus acre development announced in January 2015, and a Grand Rapids, Michigan Pyramid Campus, but those are distinct from this Las Vegas registry cluster. In December 2022 DigitalBridge and IFM Investors completed an 11 billion dollar acquisition, taking Switch private. Data center industry directories place Switch Las Vegas 4 at 4495 E Sahara Avenue, Las Vegas, NV. Sourced from DataCenterMap, which also identifies this facility by the legacy name Nevada NAP, plausibly the original 2002 Enron-facility acquisition site per Wikipedia, consistent with this locations distinct coordinates roughly 10 km from the rest of the Core Campus cluster. Single aggregator directory, not independently corroborated by a second source this session.  Switch own official locations page (fetched directly this session, https://www.switch.com/locations/) names five exascale campuses, the Citadel in Tahoe Reno, the Pyramid Campus in Grand Rapids, the Core Campus in Las Vegas, the Keep Campus in Atlanta, and the Rock Campus in Austin and Houston, but confirms no street address for any campus or building, directing visitors to a contact form instead. reading.body:
Switch Las Vegas 4 sits in Clark County as part of the Switch Las Vegas Core Campus, a cluster of eleven operating data centers spanning over 2 million square feet on the site of a former Enron facility acquired in 2002 and positioned over a nationwide fiber backbone. The operator publishes no power capacity figure for this building, so its scale relative to AI infrastructure cannot be determined from Switch's official specifications. Nevada has 26 mapped data center facilities, but only 2 publish power consumption figures, totaling 10.37 MW across the state, leaving Las Vegas 4's contribution to state capacity unknown.

Switch's exascale campuses are certified for hyperscale cloud and HPC workloads, though the specific certifications for Las Vegas 4 are not published by the operator. The facility's address and building-level specifications come from data center industry aggregator directories, not from Switch's own official locations page, which confirms no street addresses for any of its five named campuses. This lack of published power or capacity data for a major legacy facility in Nevada reflects a broader pattern on this site: most mapped facilities do not disclose their operational scale.

Without published power consumption, Las Vegas 4 cannot be ranked against other AI-scale campuses or assessed for its role in Nevada's power-constrained data center market. Its relevance to AI infrastructure scaling depends on details Switch does not make public: the power available to it, the PUE efficiency of the building, and the current utilization rate by GPU-dense workloads. The absence of these figures from an operator spec page suggests either that the facility predates or operates outside the current AI infrastructure buildout, or that Switch does not disclose capacity at the building level in Nevada.
